title: Estimates of temporary employment
text:
In this exercise, you can recreate ONS labour market analysis reported in the table EMP07 Temporary Employees. Currently, this table is updated four times a year in February, May, August and November using the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS).
Learning outcomes:

To become more familiar with QLFS datasets.
To become more familiar with the weighting variable.



The data used relates to an estimate for Oct-December 2020.
To follow the exercise, you need to access the relevant dataset from the UK Data Service: Quarterly Labour Force Survey, October - December, 2020



One you have downloaded the data, save it some where accessible.

library(tidyverse)

Apply the weight and examine the variable frequencies again.
frq(mydata1\(JBTP101, weights = mydata1\)PWT20) frq(mydata1\(FTPT, weights = mydata1\)PWT20) frq(mydata1\(INECAC05, weights = mydata1\)PWT20) frq(mydata1\(JOBTYP, weights = mydata1\)PWT20) frq(mydata1\(SEX, weights = mydata1\)PWT20)

REVIEW QUESTIONS

Do the frequencies change noticeably when the weight is applied?
Run this code to adjust the category order and labels.



RSPSSStata


mydata1$JobTmp <- rec(mydata1$JBTP101,rec="1=3;2=4;3=1;4=2;5=5;-8,-9=6")

mydata1$JobTmp <-sjlabelled::set_labels(mydata1$JobTmp, labels = c( "Seasonal work", "Done under contract for a fixed period","Agency Temping", "Casual type of work", "Some other reason"))









Create a filter to select those with a weight greater than 0.

RSPSSStata


mydata1 <- filter (mydata1, PWT20>0)









Create a variable to indicate those working part time.
::: panel-tabset ## R









:::
mydata1\(PartTime <- rec(mydata1\)FTPT,rec=“2,4=1; else=0”)
mydata1\(PartTime <-sjlabelled::set_labels(mydata1\)PartTime, labels = c(“Part Time”))


When making the table below, which cases are selected in the filter?
head(mydata1\(JOBTYP)
head(mydata1\)INECAC05)
Create the table.
#[the labels are missed doe JobTmp, crossreference with above] #for all mydata1 %>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1) %>% uncount(weights = .$PWT20) %>%
tab(JobTmp, PartTime)
#split by sex and part-time
mydata1 %>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1 & SEX==1) %>% uncount(weights = .$PWT20) %>%
tab(PartTime, JobTmp)
mydata1 %>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1 & SEX==2) %>% uncount(weights = .$PWT20) %>%
tab(PartTime, JobTmp)

REVIEW QUESTIONS

How many people are temporary employees (all and part-time) in this quarter?
How many females are in part-time temporary employment?


Note: You can check if your results match those in the ONS EMP07 dataset.
Finally, get unweighted frequencies.

RSPSSStata


mydata1 %>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1) %>%tab(JobTmp, PartTime)










REVIEW QUESTIONS
How many applicable cases to we have for the above analysis?





How many variables are there?
ncol(lfs_od20) ::: panel-tabset
